claim: Cep120 is a daughter centriole-associated ciliopathy protein.
source: Here, we show that a daughter centriole-associated ciliopathy protein, Cep120, plays a critical inhibitory role at daughter centrioles.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a characterization of Cep120

claim: Depletion of Cep120 in quiescent mouse and human cells causes accumulation of pericentriolar material (PCM) components including pericentrin, Cdk5Rap2, ninein and Cep170.
source: Depletion of Cep120 in quiescent mouse and human cells causes accumulation of pericentriolar material (PCM) components including pericentrin, Cdk5Rap2, ninein and Cep170.

claim: Loss of Cep120 leads to aberrant dynein-dependent trafficking of centrosomal proteins.

claim: Loss of Cep120 leads to dispersal of centriolar satellites.

evidence: Stated as a consequence of Cep120 loss in the abstract

claim: Cep120 helps to maintain centrosome homeostasis by inhibiting untimely maturation of the daughter centriole.

claim: Cep120 dysfunction defines a potentially new molecular defect underlying the pathogenesis of Jeune Asphyxiating Thoracic Dystrophy and Joubert syndrome.

claim: The daughter centriole was assembled in the previous cell cycle.
